import ctypes
C1=0xf4243
Cmul=0x4ec4ec4ec4ec4ec5
Cadd1=0x3b13b13b13b13b13
Ccmp=0x13b13b13b13b13b0

def cond(n):
    rdx=(n*C1)&((1<<64)-1)
    rdx=(rdx+0xb)&((1<<64)-1)
    rdx=(rdx*rdx)&((1<<64)-1)
    rdx=(rdx+0xb)&((1<<64)-1)
    rdx=(rdx*Cmul)&((1<<64)-1)
    rdx=(rdx+Cadd1)&((1<<64)-1)
    return Ccmp>=rdx, rdx
for n in [0,1,2,5,10,20,25,26,30,40,100]:
    ok, rdx=cond(n)
    print(n, ok, hex(rdx))

# find all n 0..200 for which branch to strcmp (jae)
vals=[n for n in range(0,201) if cond(n)[0]]
print('count',len(vals),'first',vals[:20],'last',vals[-20:])

args.text: Disassembly at 0x4010b0 is the main logic. If argc<=1 prints usage. Else takes argv[1] into rbx, computes strlen. There is a 64-bit arithmetic check that appears to never pass for small n (python check found no n<=200 satisfying Ccmp>=rdx), so it falls through to a strcmp against global string at 0x404030 which points to rodata "FLAG{meridian_basalt_331}". If strcmp !=0, it then checks if length==0x19 (25). If length!=25 => Wrong. If length==25, it runs a rolling XOR check: initialize edx=0xffffffa0 (i.e., -96), for i=0..24: ecx=argv1[i]; sil=(edx ^ ecx)&0xff; compare sil against byte table at 0x402040; if match all, print Correct. Solving this yields accepted input bytes = "FLAG{ferries_harbor_6628}".
